blurb: A capability is a typed interface to the outside world: a context declares it, provides it and asks for it in `given`, and the compiler wires the provider to the services that need it. A commons holds only pure declarations, so it cannot declare one. Move the capability into the context that uses it, or, for one several contexts share, into a context that exports it.
example:
commons demo

capability Logger {                     // ✗ a commons cannot declare a capability
  fn log(message: String) -> Effect[()]
}

context demo

capability Logger {                     // ✓ a context can
  fn log(message: String) -> Effect[()]
}
summary: A `capability` was declared outside a context.
